correctness.rationale: Wu's full proof gives the same Walsh--Hadamard spaces, the Rademacher lower bound, the q=2 Gaussian estimate, and the inequalities u_i<=alpha and sum u_i^2<=sqrt(n) alpha beta. For q>=2, interpolation of l2 and linfinity yields the stated Gaussian bound, while sum u_i^q<=alpha^(q-2) sum u_i^2 gives the stated (q,1)-summing estimate. The exponent comparison has a q-independent large-n threshold because the base ratio is at most one. The all-q theorem is therefore correct for every finite q>=2.
